items.title: Lando Norris reveals how Lewis Hamilton has changed his F1 championship ambitions
items.summary: Lando Norris says Lewis Hamilton's seven Formula 1 world titles have left him dissatisfied with winning just one. Norris won his maiden championship in 2025 after a hard-fought battle against his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri and a late-season threat from Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

items.title: Why Max Verstappen ended F1 practice early in Brazil – Red Bull explains
items.summary: Max Verstappen finished Friday's Formula 1 practice sessions in Sao Paulo in third place. The Dutchman occupied that position in both sessions, in fact, and was also around two and a half tenths off the fastest driver in each session, with Lando Norris topping the first one and Kimi Antonelli the second.

items.title: Fred Vasseur turns down being godfather to Charles Leclerc’s baby: “I have four children”
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Fred Vasseur has ruled himself out of becoming godfather to Charles Leclerc's daughter, joking that he already has enough children to look after. Leclerc and his wife, Alexandra, announced the birth of their first child, Bianca, on Wednesday.

items.title: F1 Brazil GP: Saturday schedule, weather forecast and how to watch
items.summary: Formula 1 heads into Saturday at Interlagos with Kimi Antonelli fastest after second practice for the Brazil Grand Prix. The newly crowned world champion set a 1m10.763s to lead Lando Norris by 0.253s, with Max Verstappen just 0.006s further back in third. George Russell was fourth ahead of Oscar Piastri, leaving Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull closely matched heading into qualifying.

items.title: McLaren’s upgrade is "a pleasant surprise" – but will it stay on the car in Brazil?
items.summary: After one of the most turbulent world championship defences since Jenson Button in 2010, Lando Norris gave McLaren’s latest batch of car upgrades a cautious thumbs-up on the Friday of the Sao Paulo GP. Norris topped the first practice session, edging out Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli by 0.082s, and was among the quickest in terms of average pace on his long runs through FP2.

items.title: Why Toto Wolff sees Ferrari clash as "déjà vu" – and why escalation may be necessary
items.summary: Following the Mexico Grand Prix, aside from Kimi Antonelli's maiden world title, one other subject has dominated the conversation in the Formula 1 paddock: the clash at Ferrari. After the incident on the opening lap of the race at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, Hamilton indicated that Ferrari had "big, big problems" to solve, before calling for in-depth discussions.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli reveals special gifts from Ayrton Senna's family ahead of F1 Brazilian GP
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has revealed the gifts he received from Ayrton Senna's family during his visit to their estate ahead of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver went to Fazenda Dois Lagos in Tatuí on Tuesday, two days after securing his maiden Formula 1 championship, and was photographed in the Lotus 98T that Senna raced in 1986.

items.title: "We failed so we had to react" - Fred Vasseur on Ferrari driver talks and Mexico F1 fallout
items.summary: Ferrari F1 chief Fred Vasseur insists he has cleared the air with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton after their highly publicised Mexican Grand Prix clash last week.

items.title: "Unacceptable downshifts" – Max Verstappen explains what's behind a recurring F1 radio complaint
items.summary: Verstappen finished the opening practice session of the Formula 1 weekend in Sao Paulo in third place, just over two tenths behind fastest man Lando Norris in the upgraded McLaren, which features a new front wing that serves as the baseline for 2027.

items.title: “Unfiltered” Lewis Hamilton is ready to exploit Charles Leclerc’s “silly” move, says Martin Brundle
items.summary: When Charles Leclerc decided to keep his foot planted across the grass at Turn 4 in Mexico rather than yield to Lewis Hamilton, he didn't just earn a five-second penalty - he sparked drama across the Ferrari team. Now, as the paddock sets up camp for the Brazilian Grand Prix, veteran Sky Sports broadcaster Martin Brundle has offered his own assessment of the Lap 1 chaos.

items.title: Colton Herta qualifies for F1 superlicence as Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on 2027 seat
items.summary: Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta has finally obtained the last remaining superlicence point required to drive in the series, but incumbent Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on his future with the squad. Herta conducted his sixth Friday practice session of the 2026 season at Interlagos, reaching the required threshold of 100km to earn his 40th superlicence point needed to race in F1.

items.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris tops FP1 as Colton Herta clinches superlicence
items.summary: Lando Norris was fastest in Free Practice 1 at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, leading Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. Norris outpaced Antonelli by 0.082s on the soft rubber with a time of 1m11.717s, while Verstappen and Hamilton were two and three tenths adrift respectively, with the top-four teams again all close together.

items.title: George Russell breaks silence on Mexican GP media absence after Mercedes fine
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has opened up about skipping his media duties after the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend. The Briton left the Mexico City circuit shortly after the race on Sunday, having congratulated his team-mate Kimi Antonelli on clinching his maiden world championship.

items.title: "Exhausted" George Russell set for Brazilian F1 grid penalty
items.summary: Mercedes driver George Russell will lose five places on Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix grid as he takes his sixth internal combustion engine of the season. Following a brace of power unit related issues earlier this year, the latest arriving after a failure at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, Russell was always going to require a sixth ICE before the end of the year.

items.title: Nico Rosberg compares Ferrari’s clashes to his own Mercedes F1 rivalry: “The instructions are not clear enough”
items.summary: Nico Rosberg knows a thing or two about racing Lewis Hamilton wheel to wheel in sister Formula 1 cars. The pair were team-mates for four years at Mercedes with an intense rivalry, and now Hamilton competes for Ferrari alongside Charles Leclerc – which has become tense at times, amid disagreements over team orders and on-track clashes.

items.title: Carlos Sainz recalls Charles Leclerc battles: “We always managed to find a solution”
items.summary: Carlos Sainz says he has "good memories" of battling Charles Leclerc at Ferrari while offering his perspective on his former Formula 1 team-mate’s fight with Lewis Hamilton in the Mexican Grand Prix. The Ferrari drivers had a fierce battle for the lead on the opening lap at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, with Leclerc attacking Hamilton through the opening corners.

items.title: Ferrari set for crunch meeting as Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc tension reaches Brazil
items.summary: Ferrari arrived at Interlagos facing a problem that, until just a few weeks ago, would have been difficult to imagine in quite this form. After a long season spent chasing competitiveness, the team finally appears to have found many of the answers that had been missing with its SF-26 Formula 1 car.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli: “My 2027 preparation starts now” after F1 title triumph
items.summary: It has been quite the week for Kimi Antonelli. After celebrating his record-breaking world title on the Mexico Grand Prix podium, where he was hoisted aloft by Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, and at the post-race party, the Italian was whisked away for sponsor commitments on Monday in the Mexican capital.

items.title: Mercedes held its breath over Kimi Antonelli’s title-winning move on Charles Leclerc
items.summary: All Kimi Antonelli needed to do at the Mexico City Grand Prix was finish ninth. Instead, the new world champion chose to clinch the title with a late-braking lunge on Charles Leclerc into Turn 1, and not everyone at Mercedes was comfortable watching it.

items.title: George Russell opens up on mental exhaustion after frustrating 2026 F1 season
items.summary: George Russell has admitted he is mentally exhausted after a season in which he has repeatedly had to overcome challenges. The Mercedes driver started 2026 as the favourite for the title, but after a string of issues outside of his control and incredible performances from his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, he watched on as the Italian became world champion in Mexico.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli admits George Russell still holds one massive advantage over him
items.summary: Let’s not sugarcoat it: George Russell had an incredibly tough 2026 campaign. With a magnet-like attraction to bad luck, the Briton spent a massive chunk of the season watching his 20-year-old team-mate storm away with the world drivers' championship.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli opens up on "very emotional" visit to Ayrton Senna's family estate
items.summary: 2026 Formula 1 champion Kimi Antonelli has opened up about his recent visit to Ayrton Senna's family home ahead of this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. The Mercedes driver went to Fazenda Dois Lagos, the Senna family estate, on Tuesday, two days after clinching the F1 title in Mexico.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli reacts to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton on Mexico podium: “I will frame it”
items.summary: Securing the 2026 world drivers' championship at just 20 years and 68 days old is a massive, history-book-shattering achievement. But for Andrea Kimi Antonelli, the most overwhelming part of the Mexico City Grand Prix did not even happen on the asphalt. It happened after the chequered flag.

items.title: Max Verstappen responds to Toto Wolff’s claim that era of "ruthless" F1 drivers is over
items.summary: Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen has responded to Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff's claim that the era of the "ruthless" F1 driver is over. After Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli clinched his maiden world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend, Wolff used the 20-year-old as an example of a new kind of champion.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli admits he questioned himself throughout his rookie campaign
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest F1 champion last weekend in Mexico, as with four rounds to go, his closest rivals lost even a theoretical chance of challenging him for the title this year. The Italian's strong performances allowed him to dominate the season - but the picture looked different last year, when he entered Formula 1 at the age of 18.

items.title: F1 Brazil GP: Friday schedule, weather forecast and how to watch
items.summary: Formula 1 heads to Interlagos this weekend with Kimi Antonelli arriving as world champion after clinching his first title at the Mexico Grand Prix. The 20-year-old became Formula 1’s youngest-ever world champion and Italy’s first since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

items.title: Oscar Piastri accepts penalty for Arvid Lindblad clash but questions F1 rules
items.summary: Oscar Piastri accepted his Mexico City Grand Prix penalty for colliding with Arvid Lindblad on the basis of the Formula 1 driving standards guidelines - but suggested that those guidelines might need tweaking for corners like the Mexican opening complex.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton admits his outspoken nature has made Ferrari move more difficult
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton has admitted that his outspoken approach has made it harder for him to fit in at Ferrari alongside Charles Leclerc, explaining that "it’s not so easy having someone like me come into a team." Hamilton, who joined the Maranello outfit at the start of the 2025 season, clashed with Leclerc on the opening lap of last weekend's Mexican Grand

items.title: Lewis Hamilton criticises Charles Leclerc: 'It was the same with Sebastian Vettel, the same with Carlos Sainz'
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams.

items.title: How raw talent Rafa Camara feels ahead of 'very surprising' F1 home debut in Brazil
items.summary: If Rafa Camara felt any nerves about making his F1 debut earlier than expected, on home soil no less, then he didn't show it. The Ferrari junior has been drafted in to replace Esteban Ocon at Haas next year, and already starts that journey this weekend after Ocon's high-profile split with the team halfway through the Mexico weekend.
